nodes.label: Freedom.to Functional Reference
nodes.rationale: Project should mimic freedom.to functionality plus additional features not present in such apps.

nodes.label: Two User-Facing Parts (Desktop + Extension)
nodes.rationale: Feature requests must be scoped: desktop code does not change extension code and vice versa.

nodes.norm_label: three-step build pipeline (popup, service worker, assemble)

nodes.label: Anti-Slop Product UI Rules
nodes.rationale: App uses product register, not marketing landing patterns: no eyebrows on every section, no section numbering, no hero-metric template, no glassmorphism default.

nodes.label: Locked Color Tokens
nodes.rationale: Green (#034f46) is the primary interactive color; pink (#f0d7ff) for selected navigation; orange (#ffa946) for focused-time cues; oxblood red (#7f1c34) only for destructive/error states; secondary text teal-tinted rather than neutral gray.

nodes.label: Anti-References
nodes.rationale: Avoid noisy gamification, guilt-heavy productivity UI, generic SaaS dashboards, decorative animations, and unclear/weak controls.

nodes.label: Extension Rebuild Rule
nodes.rationale: After EVERY big change, go to apps/extension folder and run npm run build so the dist output stays current.

nodes.label: WisprFlow UI/UX Directive
nodes.rationale: UI/UX design must follow wisprflow.com; any visual modification must use \design-extract-output as reference.
